about: The gaze bench's scenarios (README.md). Targets show on the headset's panel (gazebench.py), 64 degrees across (4:3), fixed to the head. They're fractions of the panel across (u) and down (v); 0 and 1 are 1 degree in from its edges: 31 degrees left or right, 24 up or down, the corners 37 out. Generators: grid [cols, rows] over span; edges N per edge, corners included; rays: fractions of the way from the middle to the edge along dirs directions; random N with edge_share of them on an edge; steps N, each size [lo, hi] degrees from the last, within box [yaw, pitch] degrees of the middle. background and backgrounds are the panel's brightness, 0 to 1.
prompt: Look at the dot and press the button.

scenarios.name: Edges
scenarios.about: Sixteen dots along the panel's edges and in its corners, 24 to 37 degrees out.

scenarios.name: Hold at the edges
scenarios.about: Look at an edge dot until its ring fills (3 seconds), then press: the tracker loses an eye out there.
scenarios.prompt: Keep looking at the dot. Press when its ring is full.

scenarios.name: Out from the middle
scenarios.about: Twenty-four dots on eight spokes, a third, two thirds and all the way out.

scenarios.name: Head moving
scenarios.about: Keep looking at the dot while you turn or nod your head slowly, and press while it moves.
scenarios.prompt: Keep looking at the dot while you turn or nod your head slowly. Press while your head is still moving.

scenarios.name: Light changes
scenarios.about: The panel switches between dark, bright and grey: your pupils change size.

scenarios.name: Small steps
scenarios.about: Twenty dots, each 2 to 4 degrees from the last, near the middle.

scenarios.name: After a nudge
scenarios.about: Lift the headset a little and set it back, then nine dots: how fast the tracker recovers.
scenarios.message: First lift the headset a little off your face and set it back down.

scenarios.name: Long session
scenarios.about: Sixty dots anywhere at your own pace, a few seconds apart, about six minutes: drift, slips and stale corrections.
